findings.what: The old `.trim_end()` was dropped and `indent_continuations` does not replace it, so a table message ending in `\n` (such as a toml_edit parse error) keeps that newline and the caller's `writeln!` prints a blank line; this also contradicts the updated doc comment and breaks the existing `a_message_that_ends_in_a_newline_does_not_print_a_blank_line` test.

findings.quote: let written = "no flock at /tmp/x\nto set up a flock there deliberately: mkdir -p /tmp/x";
findings.what: The emitter now adds a two-space indent to every continuation line, but the commit touches only this file, so any caller that still writes its own `\n  ` indent (the test fixture did, and `refuse_version_skew` is elsewhere) will now print four spaces.
